newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks little changed in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks little changed in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were little changed in Tuesday morning trade, with trading winding down ahead of Chinese New Year, although selective strength in some blue chips allowing the market to hold Monday's strong gains.
The Hang Seng Index was up 17.77 points, or 0.13 percent, at 13,468.84. Turnover was HK$1.33 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.

"In terms of trading range and volume, we don't expect any major movements ahead of Chinese New Year," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. The market will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the Lunar New Year holiday.
Tang said share prices were likely to resume their uptrend after the holiday, with the Hang Seng likely to challenge resistance at 14,000 in the near term.

"I think the market is going to challenge that resistance again very soon, probably towards the end of February. Quite a number of people will be buying towards the end of February ahead of the reporting season," he said.
Tang said Yamaichi had revised its 1996 earnings growth forecast for Hang Seng companies to 14 percent from a previous 13 percent and its 1997 earnings growth forecast to 16 percent from 11 percent.
Shares in Bank of East Asia rose HK$0.50 to HK$34.40 after falling HK$1.00 on Monday. HSBC Holdings was up HK$0.50 at HK$181.00 but Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.75 to HK$90.75.
Property stocks were mixed. Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$0.25 to HK$90.75 but Cheung Kong fell HK$0.50 to HK$74.00 and Henderson Land dropped HK$1.00 to HK$72.00.
Shares in Lai Sun Development fell HK$0.05 to HK$12.00. The company said it plans to issue about US$100 million in bonds convertible into shares of Asia Television Ltd.
